question: What should the first OpenClaw-owned skill permission manifest contract include, and how should declared permissions relate to install consent, signing, attestation, ClawHub trust, and runtime enforcement?
rationale: The remaining work defines a public security boundary and ecosystem contract; schema placement, trust roots, consent semantics, and enforcement timing cannot be safely chosen as autonomous cleanup.

options.title: Consolidate Design First
options.body: Keep this issue open as the product/security design anchor and use the related RFCs, PR, package, ClawHub skill, and fork as input before accepting a public manifest contract.

options.title: Land Audit-Only Metadata First
options.body: Adopt a narrow optional manifest that is explicitly inspect-only, then track consent, signing, attestation, and enforcement as later phases.

options.title: Route To ClawHub Policy
options.body: Make ClawHub or governance plugins own declarations and trust scoring unless maintainers identify a missing core API needed for enforcement or consent.

recommendation.title: Consolidate Design First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the product/security design anchor and use the related RFCs, PR, package, ClawHub skill, and fork as input before accepting a public manifest contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the clearest feature-history and latest product/security review signal for the skills and ClawHub install surface.
